answer: Each identity stakes a bond that a prism splits into colored tranches, one per shard, so withdrawing needs every tranche back at once. A random wander sends an auditor drifting through the shards each epoch: any tranche it finds unattested freezes the whole bond. N clones must also keep N squared cross-attestations alive between every pair of identities, so the farm's upkeep grows faster than its size. The ocean sets the price of depth: the deeper the total stake, the longer each tranche stays locked, and one exposed clone drains the entire refracted bond.
